column2: Darvi, pachampacha, daru; "shukla", "haimavati", "vacha" (sweet flag, whose names include "ugragandha", "shadgrantha"); "golomi", "shataparvika" (names of herbs).
Asphota, "girikarni" (clitoria); "simhasya", "vasaka" (Malabar nut), "vrisha"; "misi" (dill), "madhurika", "chhatra", "kokilaksha", "ikshura" (herbs).
Vidanga (neuter; worm-killer); "vajradru", "snuk", "snuhi", "sudha" (milkbush); "mridvika", "gostani" (grape), "draksha"; "bala", "vatyalaka" (names of plants).
Kala, "masuravidala", "triputa", "trivrit" (trivrit/turpeth); "madhuka", "klitaka", "yashtimadhuka", "madhuyashti" (liquorice).
Vidari, "kshirashukla", "ikshugandha", "kroshtri" (white variety); "gopi", "shyama", "sariva" (sarsaparilla), "ananta", "utpalasariva".
Mocha, rambha, kadali (plantain); "bhantaki", "dushpradharshini"; "sthira", "dhruva", "salaparni"; "shringi", "vrishabha", "vrisha" (herbs).
Gangeruki, "nagabala", "mushali" (Curculigo), "talamulika"; "jyotsni", "patolika", "jali", "ajashringi", "vishanika" (names of herbs).
Langalika, "agnishikha" (gloriosa lily); "tambuli", "nagavalli" (betel); "harenu", "renuka", "kaunti"; "hrivera", "divyanagara" (dry ginger).
Kalanusari, "vriddha", "ashmapushpa", "sita", "shiva" (names of fragrant plants); "saileya"; "talaparni"; "daityas"; "gandhakuti", "mura" (perfume plants).
Granthiparna, "shuka", "barhi", "vala" (fragrant roots); "tripuța", "truti" (cardamom); "shiva", "tamalaki"; "hanu", "hattavilasini".
Kuta, "nata", "dashapura", "vaneya", "paripelava" (aromatics); "tapasvini", "jatamansi" (spikenard), "prikka", "devi", "lata", "lashu".
Karchuraka, "dravidaka", "gandhamuli" and "shathi" (zedoary); "riksha-gandha", "chhagalantra", "vegi", "vriddhadaraka" (herbs).
Tundikeri, "raktaphala", "bimbika" (the ivy gourd); "pilu-parni"; "changeri", "chukrika", "ambashtha", "svarnakshiri", "himavati" (herbs).
Sahasravedhi, "chukra" (sorrel), "amlavetasa", "shatavedhi"; "jivanti", "jivani", "jiva"; "bhuninimba", "kiratika" (chiretta).
Kurchashirsha, "madhukara", "chandra", "kapivrika"; "dadrughna" (ringworm-killer, cassia), "edagaja"; "varshabhu", "shithahanini" (herbs).
Kunandati, "nikumbha", "yamani" (ajwain), "varshika"; "lashuna" (garlic), "gunjana", "arishta", "mahakanda", "rasona" (garlic names).
Varahi, "badara", "grishti"; "kakamachi", "vayasi" (black nightshade); "shatapushpa" (dill), "sitachhatra", "atichhatra", "madhura", "misi" (herbs).
Avakpushpi, "karavi"; "sarana", "prasarani"; "katambhara", "bhadrabala", "karbura", "shathi" (further herb names).
Patola (pointed gourd), "kulaka", "tikta", "karavella" (bitter gourd), "katillaka"; "kushmanda" (pumpkin); "karkaru", "varu", "karkati" (cucumber; feminine).
Ikshvaku, "katutumbi" (bitter gourd); "vishala", "indravaruni" (colocynth); "arshoghna", "shurana" (elephant-foot yam), "kanda"; "mustaka" (nut-grass), "kuruvindaka".
For bamboo: "vamsha, tvaksara, karmara, venu, maskara, tejana"; "chhatra", "atichhatra", "palaghna"; "malatrina" and "bhustrina" (grasses).
Trinaraja is the palm (tala); "ghonta", "kramuka", "puga" (areca nut); "shardula" and "dvipin" are the tiger and leopard; "haryaksha", "keshari", "hari" are the lion.
Kola, "pautri", "varaha" (boar); "koka" (wolf), "ihamriga", "vrika" (wolf); "luta" and "urnanabha" are the spider; "tantuvaya" and "markata" likewise.
Vrishchika (scorpion), "shukakita" (a stinging insect); "sarangā" and "stokaka" are the chataka bird; "krikavaku" (cock), "tamrachuda"; "pika", "kokila" (cuckoo).
For the crow: "karata", "arishta"; "baka" (crane), "kahva" are named; "koka", "chakra", "chakravaka" (ruddy goose); "kadamba", "kalahamsaka" (kinds of goose).
Patangika, "puttika" (small bees); "saragha", "madhumakshika" (honey-bee); "dvirepha", "pushpalit", "bhringa", "shatpada", "bhramara", "ali" (the bee).
Keki and "shikhin" (peacock); his cry is "keka"; "shakunti", "shakuni", "dvija" (bird); "pakshati" (feminine), "pakshamula", "chanchu" and "toti" (beak; feminine).
Gati, "uddina", "sandina" are kinds of flight; "kulaya" and "nida" are the nest; "peshi" and "kosha" the egg (neuter); "prithuka", "shavaka", "shishu" (young).

Pota, "paka", "arbhaka", "dimbha" (young one); "sandoha", "vyuhaka", "gana", "stoma", "ogha", "nikara", "vrata", "nikurambaka", "kadamba", "sanghata", "sanchaya", "vrinda", "punja", "rashi", "kuta" (words for multitude, heap).
Kshut (hunger) feminine; "kshuta" and "kshaya" masculine; "kasa" (cough), "kshavathu" (sneezing); "shotha", "shvayathu", "shopha" (swelling); "padasphota" and "vipadika" (cracked feet).
Kilasa, "sidhma", "kachchhu", "pama", "vicharchika" (skin diseases); "kotha", "mandalaka", "kushtha" (leprosy), "shvitra", "dru"; and "arshas" (piles).
Anaha and "vibandha" (constipation); "grahani" (dysentery), "pravahika" (diarrhoea); "shukra" is semen, the vital seed; "palala" is flesh, "kravya" and "amisha" raw meat.
Hridaya (heart), "hanu" (jaw); "meda", "vapa", "vasa" (fat); "paschadgriva" (nape), "shira" (vein), "manya"; "nadi" and "dhamani" (vessel, artery).
Tilaka (mole), "mastishka" (brain), "drushika" (the secretion of the eyes); "antra" (intestine), "puri"; "gulma" (spleen-mass), "pliha" (spleen, masculine); "vasnasa".
Snayu (sinew, feminine); "kalakhanda", "yakrit" (liver) are alike; "karpura" and "kapala" (skull, neuter); "kikasa" and "sankulya" are bones.
Kankala is the bones of the body; "kaseruka" the bones of the back; "karoti" the skull-bones (feminine); "parshuka" the rib bones.
Anga, "pratika", "avayava" (limb); "sharira", "varshma", "vigraha" (body); "kata" (masculine), "shronifalaka", "kati", "shroni" (hip, waist).
Nitamba is the hinder part of a woman's waist; "jaghana" (neuter) the front; "kupaka" lies on the buttocks; "kakundara" is the dimple.
Sphich (the two buttocks); "kati-protha"; "upastha"; "bhaga" and "yoni" (female organ); "shishna", "medhra", "mehana", "shepha" (male organ).
Pichanda, "kukshi", "jathara", "udara", "tunda" (belly); "kucha", "stana" (breasts); "chuchuka" is the nipple; "kroda" is the chest between the arms.
Skandha (shoulder), "bhujashiras", "amsha"; "sandhi" (joint) and "jatru" (collar-bone); "kararuha" and "nakha", "nakhara" (nails).
Pradesha, tala, gokarna — measures of the spread hand with the forefinger and the others; with thumb and little finger extended, "vitasti" is twelve finger-breadths.
Peta, "pratala", "prahasta" are the open palm with fingers spread; "ratni" is the fist closed, "aratni" the one with little finger extended (cubit-measures).
Kambugriva (neck with three folds); "avatu", "ghata", "krikatika" (nape); "chibuka" is the chin below the lip; "ganda" (cheek), "gala" (throat), "hanu" (jaw).
Apanga is the outer corner of the eyes; "kataksha" a sidelong glance; "chikura", "kuntala", "bala" (hair); "pratikarma", "prasadhana" (toilette).
Akalpa, "veSha", "nepathya" (dress, costume); "pratyaksha"; "chudamani" is the crest-jewel; "tarala" is the central gem of a necklace.
Karnika, "talapatra" (ear ornaments); "lambana", "lalantika" (pendants); "manjira", "nupura" (anklet, on the foot); "kinkini" is a small bell.
Dairghya, "ayama" (length); "aroha" (height), "parinaha" (girth), "vishalata" (breadth); "patachchara" is worn-out cloth; "samvyana", "uttariya" (upper garment).
Rachana (arrangement), "parispanda", "abhoga", "paripurnata" (fullness); "samudgaka", "sampuṭaka" (casket); "pratigraha", "patadgraha" (spittoon).
Chashala is the sacrificial post's ring; "sthandila" and "chatvara" are the ground for sacrifice; "amiksha" is curd formed when hot milk is mixed with curds.
Prishadajya is ghee with curds; "paramanna" is "payasa" (milk-rice); "upakrita" is the animal consecrated by mantra and slain in the sacrifice.
Paramparaka, "samana", "prokshana" (sprinkling) have the sense of slaying; "puja, namasya, apachiti, saparya, archa, arhana" are alike (worship).
Parivasya, "shushrusha", "paricharya", "upasana" (service, attendance); "niyama", "vrata" (vow); fasting and the like is merit-producing.
The first "kalpa" is the primary rule; the "anukalpa" is the lesser substitute; in a "kalpa" know the procedure and order; "viveka" is discernment, separateness of self.
Upakarana is taking up scripture after a purifying rite; "bhikshu", "parivrat", "karmandi", "parasharya", "maskari" are names of ascetics.
Rishi are those of true speech; "snataka" and "aplutavrati"; those who have conquered the host of senses are "yatis" and "yatayas".
Yama is the regular duty that depends on bodily means; "niyama" is an occasional duty requiring an extraneous means; "brahmabhuya", "brahmatva", "brahmasayujya" (union with Brahman).
Tuna, "upasanga", "tunira", "nishanga", "ishudhi" (quiver, masculine/feminine); "asi", "rishti", "nistrimsha", "karavala", "kripana" (sword).
Saru is a sword's hilt; "ili" is a sword-blade; "karapalika" a dagger; "kuthara" an axe; "sudhiti"; "churika" and "asiputrika" (small knives).
Prasa and "kunta" are known as spears; "sarvala"; "tomara" (feminine); "vaitalika" and "bodhakara" are bards, "magadha" and "vandin" praise-singers.
Samshaptaka are warriors sworn not to retreat from battle; "pataka" and "vaijayanti" are banners; "ketana" and "dhvaja" are flags.
Aham-purvika (feminine) is "I first, I first"; "aham-ahamika" is mutual self-assertion, the pride of one against the other.
Shakti, "parakrama", "prana", "shaurya", "sthama", "sahas", "bala" (power); "murchha", "kashmala", "moha" (swoon); "mardana" and "pidana" (crushing).
Abhyavaskandana, "abhyasadana" (assault); "vijaya", "jaya" (victory); "nirvasana", "sanjnapana", "sarana", "pratighatana" (killing, driving out).
Panchata, "kaladharma", "dishtanta", "pralaya", "atyaya" (death); "vish" and "bhumispriksh" are the Vaishyas; "vritti", "vartana", "jivana" (livelihood).
Farming and the like are known as livelihoods; "kusida" is usury; "uddhara" is lending money; "kanisha" is the ear of grain, "sasyamanjari".
Kimsharu is the awn of grain; "stamba" and "gutsa" are clumps of grass; "dhanya" is rice and grain; "stambakari", "kadangara"; "vapa" (sowing).
Beans such as "masha" are "shamidhanya"; barley and the like are "shukadhanya"; "nivara" and similar are grass-grains; "shurpa" is the winnowing basket, "prasphotana".
Syuta and "prasevaka" (bag), "kandola", "pita", "kataka", "kinjaka" (baskets) are alike; "rasavati" is the kitchen, the cooking-place, "mahanasa".
Paurogava is the chief cook; "supakara", "vallava" (cooks); "aralika", "andhasika", "suda", "audanika", "guna" (kitchen servants).
Ambarisha (neuter) is a frying-pan; "bhrashta" (masculine); "karkari", "alu", "galantika" (water pots); "alinjara", "manika" (jars); "sushavi", "krishnajiraka" (cumin).

Aranala is sour gruel; "kulmasha" (half-cooked grain); "vahlika", "hingu", "ramatha" (asafoetida); "nisha", "haridra" (turmeric, yellow; feminine); "khanda" (sugar), "matsyandi", "phanita" (molasses).
Kurchika is a preparation of milk; "snigdha", "masrina", "chikkana" (smooth); "prithuka", "chipitaka" (flattened rice); "dhana" are parched barley grains.
Jemana, "lepa", "ahara" (food, meal); "maheyi" and "saurabhi" are the cow; those who carry the yoke and the like are "yugya", "prasangya", "shatakaka" (draught-animals).
Chirasuta and "vashkayani" are cows that calved long ago; "navasutika" has newly calved; "sandhini" is a cow mounted by a bull; "vehat" is one that has aborted.
